items.program: Master of Science in Finance (combination bachelor's/master's)

gre.detail: MSF Program does not require a GMAT nor GRE score. SAT/ACT from UF undergrad record are electronically accessible; minimum expected SAT combined math+reading 1350/1600 or ACT math 31/36.

gmat.detail: Applicants may submit a GMAT score to enhance the application; any GMAT received is included in comprehensive review. Program does not require GMAT.

toefl.detail: Applications sought only from current UF undergraduates; English proficiency not listed on MSF page for this pathway.

ielts.detail: Same as TOEFL — UF undergrad combo pathway only.

english.waiver: N/A for eligible UF undergraduates (program does not admit external/international applicants).

gpa.detail: Keep overall GPA above a 3.6; minimum 3.6 overall GPA expected for application. Average application GPA for MSF classes of 2026 and 2027 was 3.91.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Two letters of recommendation emailed directly to Mrs. Hunt (Tayla.Hunt@warrington.ufl.edu) by recommenders.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Statement of purpose describing chosen career path and firms of interest; focus on junior summer internship targets with accompanying Excel/Word table of firms, caliber criteria, and recruitment process.

resume.detail: Resume formatted for finance industry; must include all post-high school education and employment and ongoing international affiliations/research funding per Florida Statute.

transcripts.detail: UF transcripts available electronically to MSF Admissions Committee from Student Information System; applicants do not need to order/email transcripts.

interview.detail: Candidates selected to interview should demonstrate characteristics appropriate for graduate business courses and qualifications expected by firms in their statement of purpose.

applicationFee.detail: MSF program page does not state an application fee. Warrington specialized master's materials reference the UF Graduate School application; MBA section of masters-admissions page cites $30, but MSF combo page itself is silent.

other: RESTRICTED: applications only sought from current UF undergraduates (combination bachelor's/master's).
Pre-application form after first-year spring grades; full application in second year.
SAT/ACT used from UF record (not GRE/GMAT).
Complete required summer credits before third year; FIN/general business majors must complete 4000-level FIN prerequisites.
applicationRequirements.advice: External and international applicants are not eligible for classic florida-msf; see florida-msft (MS Finance and Technology) for an open path. Documented here for eligible UF undergrads only.
sources: MS Finance program / how to apply

gre.detail: Test scores not required for admission. Applicants may submit GRE to demonstrate potential; ASU does not accept GRE General Test at-home exam. Institution code 4007.

gmat.detail: Test scores not required. Optional GMAT may be submitted; W. P. Carey GMAT code 0GZ-1R-80.

toefl.detail: Required for non-native English speakers. ASU graduate minimum: TOEFL iBT 80 if taken before Jan 21, 2026; minimum 4 on new scale if on/after Jan 21, 2026. W. P. Carey states its graduate minimums may be higher than ASU but does not publish a program-specific number on the MS-FIN page. Does not accept TOEFL iBT Home Edition if taken prior to Jan 21, 2026, Paper Edition, or Essentials.

ielts.detail: IELTS Academic overall band at least 6.5 (ASU graduate minimum). W. P. Carey may set higher unpublished program minimums.

english.waiver: ASU English proficiency exemptions (citizenship list, U.S. degree, medium-of-instruction, etc.) via Admission Services forms after applying. See admission.asu.edu English proficiency page.

gpa.detail: ASU Degree Search: minimum cumulative GPA of 3.00 in last 60 semester / 90 quarter hours of first bachelor's, or 3.00 in applicable master's.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: One letter of recommendation; provide recommender name, affiliation, and work email. Should comment on motivation, commitment, achievements, work experience, and likely success (Degree Search).

statementOfPurpose.detail: Admission essay / short-answer question responses in graduate application. Personal statements will not be accepted and will delay review. Essay prompts are in the graduate application.

resume.detail: Current resume must include positions held and clearly indicate dates of employment in Month/Year format.

transcripts.detail: Unofficial OK at application; if admitted, official transcripts from every college/university awarding bachelor's or higher required. ASU attendees need not submit ASU transcripts. International: original language + official English translation.

interview.detail: Interview not mentioned on MS-FIN application-process page.

applicationFee.waivers: Military and Citizen Service: U.S. Military, Teach for America, Peace Corps, or AmeriCorps — email wpcareymasters@asu.edu before applying. Domestic fee $70.
applicationFee.detail: $70 domestic; $115 international. Non-refundable; applications not processed until fee received.

other: Bachelor's or master's from regionally accredited institution in business/management, economics, statistics, CS, or other STEM areas (Degree Search).
Three-year undergraduate degree with no additional coursework may qualify — contact wpcareymasters@asu.edu.
$500 non-refundable enrollment deposit after admission.
applicationRequirements.advice: International priority Round II Feb 1, 2027; international final Round III Apr 1, 2027. Submit English proof and allow visa/financial guarantee time after admission.

gre.detail: GMAT or GRE is not required. Optional; strongly recommended if GPA under 3.0 per FAQs. Scores valid up to five years. GRE code 4859.

gmat.detail: Not required; optional additional data point. GMAT code 0DP-7R-40.

toefl.detail: International students if applicable. Minimum TOEFL iBT 80/120 or 4.0/6.0 (new scale). Valid up to two years. Institution code 4859.

ielts.detail: IELTS Academic minimum overall 7, with no individual module less than 6. Electronic scores only from test center.

english.waiver: Waived if undergraduate or graduate degree from a U.S. institution or institution where English was the sole language of instruction per World Higher Education Database (WHED).

gpa.detail: No minimum GPA published on admissions page. FAQs recommend GMAT/GRE if GPA under 3.0 as evidence of quantitative/verbal skills.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Two essays (one video and one written).

transcripts.detail: Official transcripts from all institutions attended to earn an undergraduate degree (English translation if applicable). WES evaluations not accepted (FAQ).

applicationFee.waivers: Available for attending select recruitment events. Fees paid prior to waiver approval are non-refundable.

other: 3-year bachelor's (except UK) generally needs additional master's/PGD for U.S. 4-year equivalence — see FAQs.
Recommended: quantitative coursework (calculus, statistics, economics), accounting exposure, strong analytics.
applicationRequirements.advice: International students must submit all materials including LORs by applicable deadline for visa processing. Round 3 Feb 1 priority for UCI housing / recommended for internationals; Round 4 Apr 1 international student deadline.

gre.detail: Not required if: undergrad GPA ≥3.3 with quantitative major; OR master's in technical/quantitative field with GPA ≥3.0; OR advanced degree (MBA, JD, MD, PhD). Otherwise GMAT or GRE required. Waiver form available.

gmat.detail: Same conditional policy as GRE — optional if waiver criteria met; otherwise required. Contact Shea McCormick with questions.

toefl.detail: For applicants whose native language is not English and who graduated from a non-U.S. institution in a country where English is not official. Minimum 90 on 120 scale or 4.5 on 1–6 scale. VSB TOEFL code 2959.

ielts.detail: IELTS Academic minimum 7. Send to Villanova University – Villanova School of Business.

english.waiver: U.S. institution graduates not required. Also: undergraduate degree in the U.S. or lived in the U.S. for the past two years — contact Grad Business Office for waiver.

gpa.detail: No absolute minimum GPA published for admission. Undergrad GPA ≥3.3 (quantitative major) is one path to GMAT/GRE optional status.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: One letter; professional preferred (current/previous supervisor; internships OK). Academic OK if no work experience. No personal/family recommendations.

statementOfPurpose.detail: One essay on short- and long-term career plans; how Villanova MSF meets professional goals; academic/personal/professional motivation.

resume.detail: Business resume with educational and professional information.

transcripts.detail: One official transcript from each postsecondary institution with ≥9 credit hours. Unofficial OK for review; official degree-bearing before classes. Non-U.S. studies: WES or ECE course-by-course evaluation required (no other services).

interview.detail: Interview not listed on MSF admissions page.

applicationFee.detail: Non-refundable $65, paid by credit card on online application.

other: Program starts in July (full-time ~11 months).
International deadline Round 2 Jan 15 recommended for visa.
Econometrics / macro / math of economics recommended prerequisites (not required).
applicationRequirements.advice: Apply by Round 2 (Jan 15) as international. WES/ECE course-by-course required before review for non-U.S. credentials. STEM OPT extension eligible after program.

gre.detail: GMAT or GRE not required if applicant has or will have undergraduate degree from a U.S. college/university prior to enrollment. Applicants from colleges/universities outside the U.S. must submit valid GMAT or apply for GMAT waiver. Scores ≤5 years. GRE code 6998.

gmat.detail: Not required for U.S. bachelor's holders/expected graduates. Required for non-U.S. institution applicants unless waiver granted via waiver form. GMAT code XM7-2D-68.

toefl.detail: Non-U.S. citizen applicants (and U.S. citizens with extensive international study) must submit English proficiency. Mendoza MSF page accepts TOEFL; does not publish a minimum score. Mendoza TOEFL code 2456. ND Graduate School publishes TOEFL iBT 80 (pre-Feb 2026; Speaking ≥23) or 4.5 avg / no section <4.0 (updated) — cite Grad School separately; confirm with Mendoza if program-specific floor differs.

ielts.detail: IELTS accepted on Mendoza MSF page; minimum not published there. ND Graduate School lists IELTS 7.0 composite.

english.waiver: May be waived if completed at least six full-time semesters or nine full-time quarters at a university where English is the primary language (transcripts verify; committee may request more).

gpa.detail: No minimum GPA stated on MSF apply page.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: One recommendation; someone familiar with professional or academic background who can offer detailed assessment.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Written statement ≤500 words: detailed post-master's career plans; how background + Notre Dame studies equip you; short- and long-term goals with industry and function.

resume.detail: One-page resume summarizing education, work experience, skills, accomplishments.

transcripts.detail: From all colleges/universities attended including summer and graduate study. International transcripts need official English translation. Unofficial OK for application; official final with proof of graduation before enrollment if admitted. Degree audits not accepted.

interview.detail: Video assessment required after application submission (Admissions Committee questions); must complete to move forward. Not framed as optional invitation-only live interview.

applicationFee.waivers: U.S. Active Duty Military or Veterans; current/former Peace Corps; current/former Teach for America — contact msf.business@nd.edu.
applicationFee.detail: $50 non-refundable; pay via application status page after submit. Application incomplete until paid.

other: Applicant Snapshot: required 4-slide PDF deck (no audio/video).
Optional supplemental essay for additional context.
Also accepts PTE Academic and Duolingo for English (mins not on Mendoza MSF page).
applicationRequirements.advice: International applicants strongly encouraged to apply by Round 2 for visa timing. Non-U.S. undergrad degree holders: plan GMAT or GMAT waiver early.
sources: ND Graduate School international English (mins reference)

items.program: Master of Science in Finance (MS FIN)

gre.detail: GMAT/GRE not required; optional submission. Score used only if provided. GRE school code R6897.

gmat.detail: Optional; use listed GMAT program codes when submitting.

toefl.detail: International applicants: TOEFL minimum 80 iBT; score ≤2 years from application date. Institutional code 6897 (FAQ).

ielts.detail: IELTS minimum 6.5. Also accepts PTE minimum 67.

english.waiver: Waived if bachelor's or master's earned through instruction/examination in English, or native country's primary language is English (UTD list). U.S. degree holders waived.

gpa.detail: No hard minimum published. Cumulative GPA used in holistic review; currently average admitted GPA is 3.3 (FAQ / MS admissions).

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: MS Finance FAQ and MS Finance Cohort page: one letter of recommendation (professional; no specific format). Note: general Jindal MS Programs Admission page states three LORs (or one if ≥2 years post-baccalaureate experience) — program-specific MS Finance materials say one.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Personal objectives statement — one-page typed essay outlining academic interests and goals (cohort page: one-page typed; general MS page: one-page double-spaced).

resume.detail: Detailed résumé of work history; work experience not required for MS degrees.

transcripts.detail: Official transcripts from all colleges/universities; international degree certificate if applicable. Unofficial OK for decision; official before enrollment.

interview.detail: Interview not mentioned on MS Finance FAQ or Cohort application section.

applicationFee.waivers: UT Dallas students/alumni automatic waiver; military and listed Graduate Application Fee Waiver Program (U.S. citizens/PRs) per Graduate Admissions deadlines-and-fees page.
applicationFee.detail: $75 non-refundable via application/Applicant Portal (UTD Graduate Admissions).

other: Calculus knowledge required for MS Finance; OPRE 6303 available if missing.
Fall deadline May 1 (FAQ); Cohort page notes Apr 30 foreign / May 31 domestic for cohort track — confirm track.
Also accepts PTE (min 67).
applicationRequirements.advice: International: submit English scores and credentials early; May 1 fall deadline (or cohort foreign Apr 30). STEM program; ISSO handles I-20.
sources: UTD Graduate Admissions deadlines and fees

gre.detail: Applicants must submit GMAT or GRE from within past five years. Full-time and part-time MSF applicants may request GMAT/GRE waiver consideration before completing application. GRE school code 3033. Class profile Fall 2026 avg GRE 319 (context only).

gmat.detail: GMAT Exam or GMAT Focus accepted. School code 44x-J5-96. Waiver request available for FT and PT MSF. No preference between GMAT/GRE. Fall 2026 FT avg GMAT Focus 644 (context).

toefl.detail: Non-U.S. citizens/PRs: TOEFL iBT traditional minimum 100; TOEFL iBT (New) minimum 5. Scores within past two years. MyBest not accepted.

english.waiver: Completed four-year bachelor's or two-year master's (or higher) entirely at English-medium institution (MOI on transcript or official letter); OR ≥2 years full-time post-degree work in U.S. or country where English is official language. No separate waiver form required if eligible.

gpa.detail: No minimum GPA required (FAQ). Fall 2026 FT average undergrad GPA 3.58 (profile).

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: One required; up to three accepted. Academic (professors) or professional (supervisors/managers). Online recommendation forms.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Required essay ≤500 words: past experiences, short- and long-term goals, why MSF at Boston College. Optional essay for uncovered aspects.

resume.detail: Resume or CV outlining education and professional experience including part-time/internships with months and years; recommend 1–2 pages.

transcripts.detail: Four-year bachelor's (or equivalent) required. Self-reported transcript at application; official if admitted. Non-U.S.: English translation + third-party degree verification (SpanTran/TEC or WES) if admitted.

interview.detail: MSF application materials page does not list an interview. FAQ interview-by-invitation applies to Ph.D. programs, not MSF.

applicationFee.waivers: Reapplicants: contact Graduate Admissions before submitting for fee waiver (FAQ).

other: Quantitative Finance STEM track selected on enrollment form after admission (not separate application).
Spring 2027 entry available for Quantitative Track only.
Fifth-year BC undergrad pathway exists with separate requirements page.
applicationRequirements.advice: International applicants strongly encouraged to apply by starred early deadlines for visa. Part-time not F-1 sponsored. Quant track STEM OPT extension path.

gre.detail: GRE or GMAT required (waivers available). Scores within past five years. ETS/GRE code 4053. Waiver paths include business bachelor's from AACSB/EQUIS school; BS in finance/accounting/business analytics/STEM; ≥4 units stats/calculus B+ or better; certain professional licenses; 5+ years quantitative work; partner-institution alumni — email admissions@cgu.edu when application started.

gmat.detail: GMAT or GRE required with same waiver policy. GMAT code DZK-QS-08.

toefl.detail: Non-native English speakers: TOEFL minimum 95 (old scale) / 5 (new score scale) for direct entry. Code 4053. Lower scores may enter via International Scholars Program (TOEFL 75/4).

ielts.detail: IELTS 7.0 with no sub-score less than 6.5 for direct entry. Also PTE 66; Duolingo 125 for direct entry.

english.waiver: Citizens/PRs of English sole-official-language countries; degree from U.S. or those countries; recent U.S. academic English pre-master's/bridge; or degree where English is a primary language of instruction for majority of courses with documentation.

gpa.detail: No GPA minimum published on MSF page or Drucker 2027 how-to-apply news (Associate Dean: no score cutoffs / no GPA minimums).

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Optional. If submitting, recommender emails letter to admissions@cgu.edu with applicant full name. News post: no longer required.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Applicant questionnaire: five short responses ≤100 words each (motivation; goals; alignment with Drucker ideals; contribution; biggest challenge). Upload to status page after online application.

transcripts.detail: Sealed official transcript from every undergrad/grad institution that granted a degree; electronic to admissions@cgu.edu OK. Unofficial for review; official upon admission. Bachelor's from regionally accredited college required.

interview.detail: Required for admission upon review of application; decision not issued until interview complete. Drucker news: every applicant who completes an application is interviewed.

other: Prerequisite: Financial Accounting (coursework B or better at accredited institution or approved equivalent) before entering.
Fall 2027: priority Feb 1, 2027; international final June 1, 2027 (program page) / June 5, 2027 (Drucker news table — slight date conflict; verify closer to cycle).
STEM designated.
applicationRequirements.advice: International final deadline earlier than domestic for visa. Reach out to Drucker recruiters early; interview is mandatory after complete file.

gre.detail: GMAT or GRE optional. Committee may request official scores if unable to decide from submitted materials. Institution code 1836. Upload unofficial score to portal while awaiting official.

gmat.detail: Optional; same policy as GRE. Official to UIUC code 1836.

toefl.detail: Non-native speakers without Graduate College exemption: Full-status TOEFL iBT 103 (scores prior to 1/21/26) or 5.0 (scores after 1/20/26). Limited-status: 79 / 4.0. Official scores required; dated after Aug 1, 2025. Code 1836.

ielts.detail: Full-status IELTS Academic 7.5; limited-status 6.5. Also Duolingo full 135 / limited 115.

english.waiver: Graduate College English proficiency exemptions apply (see Grad College English Proficiency Requirements). Limited-status admits take English Placement Test on arrival; may require ESL coursework.

gpa.detail: Illinois Graduate College minimum: GPA 3.0 (A=4.0) for last two years of undergraduate study. Programs may require higher; MSF page does not state a higher floor. Optional essay strongly recommended if GPA ≤3.0.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: Two references from academic and/or professional sources; signed and dated. Late LORs (>7 days after deadline) move application to next round.

statementOfPurpose.detail: Academic Statement of Purpose 300–500 words total (background prep; how program helps goals; academic interests). Plus two short personal statements ≤250 words each.
statementOfPurpose.alsoKnownAs: Academic Statement of Purpose + personal statements

resume.detail: Professional résumé ≤2 pages (education, work, internships, training, associations, leadership).

transcripts.detail: Most recent unofficial transcripts with name, institution, legend/scale. Diploma/certificate of degree if bachelor's earned. Official upon arrival if admitted. Check Grad College country requirements for U.S. bachelor's equivalence.

interview.detail: Required video essay component (3 randomly assigned questions, ~3 minutes). Live interview by invitation only if materials insufficient; decisions may be made with or without interview.

applicationFee.detail: Non-refundable $90 for domestic and international. Cannot be processed without payment.

other: Select program Finance → Finance - MS in Grad College portal.
Optional essay available; scholarship acknowledgment in Financial Aid section for merit/need consideration.
Passport/funding proof for internationals only after admission offer.
applicationRequirements.advice: Fall 2027 Round 4 May 5, 2027 is final deadline for international applicants needing a new visa. Apply early for scholarship consideration.

items.program: Master of Science in Finance (4+1 / combination)

gre.detail: Minimum 50th percentile on quantitative portion. Waived for those with GPA of 3.5 or higher in STEM, Business, or ECON majors. Program details: Sophomore Start also notes minimum 50th percentile GRE Q with minimum GPA 3.0 emphasis.

gmat.detail: GMAT not mentioned on 4+1 MS Finance hub or program-details pages; GRE is the listed standardized test.

toefl.detail: Program restricted to current Texas A&M undergraduates; English proficiency exams not listed among admission requirements.

english.waiver: N/A for eligible TAMU undergraduates (external/international N/A).

gpa.detail: Minimum GPA 3.25 overall; 3.5 for FINC majors (hub). Program-details Sophomore Start text also cites minimum GPA 3.0 with GRE Q ≥50th percentile — hub list is the primary published requirement set.

lettersOfRecommendation.detail: LOR not listed among published admission requirements on hub or program-details pages.

interview.detail: Program-details: Apply through April 15 to be interviewed in the spring semester. Not stated whether every applicant is interviewed.

applicationFee.detail: Application fee not stated on 4+1 MS Finance hub or program-details pages.

other: RESTRICTED: all applicants must currently be enrolled as undergraduates at Texas A&M University (College Station).
Attend information session (listed requirement).
Prerequisites (B or better) due after admission by end of spring following application: ACCT 209/229/640 and ECON 202 or 203.
Sophomore Start and Senior Start pathways; few spots for seniors (senior start needs ≥1 commercial internship).
applicationRequirements.advice: External and international applicants are not eligible for classic tamu-msf 4+1; see tamu-qfin for a separate open quantitative path. Pages currently emphasize Fall 2026 entry cycles; 2027–28 cycle opens Apr 1, 2027.
